title: Organise counts, inventories and next-number
chapter: Make every digit obey both its jobs
goal: Count digits place by place, and know whether you are counting numbers or occurrences.

scenes.visual: A strip of numbers 1 to 30. All the 2s light up, including both digits of 22.
scenes.narration: "How many numbers contain a two?" and "How many twos are written?" are different questions. Twenty-two is one number, but it contains two twos. Decide which you are counting, then count one place at a time.

scenes.visual: A messy tally with a repeated number counted wrongly; beside it two neat columns "units place" and "tens place".
scenes.narration: Counting straight through a long list is slow and error-prone. Counting each place separately is quick, and repeated digits take care of themselves.

scenes.visual: Numbers 1 to 100 in a ten by ten grid. Question: "How many times is the digit 7 written?"
scenes.narration: All the whole numbers from one to one hundred are written out. How many times is the digit seven written? Pause and think about the units place first.

scenes.visual: The column 7, 17, 27, up to 97 lights up: ten cells. Label "units place: 10".
scenes.narration: In the units place, seven appears once in every ten numbers: seven, seventeen, twenty-seven, up to ninety-seven. That is ten times.

scenes.visual: The row 70 to 79 lights up: ten cells. Label "tens place: 10". The cell 77 glows in both colours. Total 20.
scenes.narration: In the tens place, seven appears in seventy to seventy-nine: ten times. Altogether the digit seven is written twenty times. Seventy-seven was counted once in each place, which is correct, because it has two sevens.

scenes.visual: Same grid; the lit cells are counted as cells: 19. Label "numbers containing a 7".
scenes.narration: Now the other question: how many numbers contain a seven? The column has ten numbers and the row has ten, but seventy-seven is in both. Ten plus ten minus one is nineteen.

scenes.visual: Page numbers 1 to 9 use 9 digits; 10 to 99 use 180 digits; a counter totals 189.
scenes.narration: A related skill is counting all the digits. Numbering pages one to ninety-nine uses nine digits for the single-digit pages, and two digits each for the ninety pages from ten to ninety-nine. That is nine plus one hundred and eighty: one hundred and eighty-nine digits.

scenes.visual: Lines: "Numbers or occurrences?", "Count each place separately", "For numbers, do not double count overlaps".
scenes.narration: Decide whether you are counting numbers or occurrences. Count each place separately. For numbers, remove any overlap. Notebook challenge: how many times is the digit three written in the numbers from one to fifty?

notebook_exercise: How many times is the digit 3 written in the numbers from 1 to 50?
notebook_answer: Units: 3, 13, 23, 33, 43 (5 times); tens: 30 to 39 (10 times); total 15.
